title: Aries Moon:
who you match with.
summary: How a Vedic match reads an Aries Moon against all twelve signs: Mars and his friends, the strongest matches, the hard one, and what a full match adds.
film: Aries: who are you compatible with?
imageAlt: Maya holding an Aries flag while a ram and a lion stand together under a Top match: Leo ribbon
inside: How a Vedic match is scored, and the two tests that need only your Moon signs
Your four strongest matches and why each one is read that way
All twelve signs against an Aries Moon, in one table
What to do when your person is on the hard side of the table
intro: The film names five signs in sixty seconds: Leo, Sagittarius, Cancer, Libra and Virgo. This guide shows where those names come from, and reads an Aries Moon against all twelve signs, so you can look up the one you actually care about.

One thing first. Everything here goes by Moon sign, yours and theirs, and it is what the tradition reads as a tendency, never a verdict on two real people. Signs are the start of a Vedic match, not the whole of it. The last sections say what the rest is and how much weight to give this.

sections.label: How a match is read
title: Eight tests,
two from the signs.
paragraphs: A traditional Vedic match compares the Moon in two charts through eight tests, worth thirty-six points together. Six of them need the exact birth star of each person. Two can be read from the Moon signs alone, and between them they carry twelve of the thirty-six points. Those two are what a sign-by-sign guide like this one can honestly tell you.

items.name: The rulers' friendship
items.text: Every sign has a ruling planet, and the planets have fixed friends, neutrals and enemies. Your ruler is Mars. Mars counts the Sun, the Moon and Jupiter as friends, Venus and Saturn as neutral, and Mercury as his one enemy. Two people whose rulers are friends are read as understanding each other without much effort.

items.name: The distance between the signs
items.text: Count from your sign to theirs. Signs that are the same, opposite, third and eleventh, or fourth and tenth from each other are read as easy. Second and twelfth, fifth and ninth, and sixth and eighth are the three difficult distances. The usual rule sets a difficult distance aside when the two rulers are friends, or are the same planet.

items.name: Leo
items.text: The Sun rules Leo, and the Sun and Mars are friends in both directions, the best score the first test gives. Leo is fire, like you. It is read as big, warm, loud love between two people who both expect to lead. The work in this match is taking turns.

items.name: Sagittarius
items.text: Jupiter rules Sagittarius, and Jupiter and Mars are friends in both directions too. Another fire sign, and the one said to match your pace. Sagittarius is read as hard to offend, which matters with a temper as quick as yours: they tend to laugh, and you tend to calm down.

items.name: Cancer
items.text: The Moon rules Cancer and Mars counts the Moon as a friend. Cancer sits fourth from Aries, an easy distance, and the fourth is the place of home. This is read as your soft place: someone who looks after you and gives you somewhere to come back to. Go gently, because Cancer feels a sharp word for longer than you do.

items.name: Libra
items.text: Libra is the sign directly opposite yours, the seventh, which is the place of the partner in any chart. Mars and Venus are neutral to each other, so this is not an automatic friendship. It is read as attraction: each has what the other lacks, your directness and their tact.

sections.label: All twelve signs
title: Find
your person.
paragraphs: Look up their Moon sign, not their Sun sign. Each line gives their ruler, how the two tests read against an Aries Moon, and what that is said to feel like.

rows.note: The same sign and the same ruler. You understand each other at once. Two quick tempers in one room is the thing to manage.
Ruled by Venus, neutral to Mars, and the signs sit second and twelfth, a difficult distance. You move fast and Taurus does not. Read as a match that needs patience from you.
Ruled by Mercury, the one planet Mars counts as an enemy, but the signs sit third and eleventh, an easy distance. Read as fun and lively company with arguments about small things.
Ruled by the Moon, a friend of Mars, at an easy distance. Your soft place.
Ruled by the Sun, a friend in both directions. Fifth and ninth is a difficult distance, set aside here because the rulers are friends.
Ruled by Mercury, and the signs sit sixth and eighth, the hardest distance, with no friendship to set it aside. Read as two people who do everything differently.
Your opposite sign, the place of the partner. Rulers neutral. Read as a strong pull and a real difference in style.
Also ruled by Mars. Sixth and eighth is a difficult distance, set aside here because you share a ruler. Read as deep understanding and strong feelings on both sides.
Ruled by Jupiter, a friend in both directions. The difficult distance is set aside by that friendship. The one who keeps pace.
Ruled by Saturn, who counts Mars as an enemy, at an easy distance. Read as respect and shared ambition, at two very different speeds.
Also ruled by Saturn, at an easy distance. Read as a good friendship first. Warmth can take time to show.
Ruled by Jupiter, a friend of Mars. Second and twelfth is a difficult distance, set aside by that friendship. Read as kind and forgiving, with Pisces softening your edges.

after: Where a difficult distance is set aside, astrologers still look at it in a full match. It is treated as eased, not erased.

sections.label: The hard one
title: Virgo,
and why it is not a no.
paragraphs: Virgo comes out lowest on both tests: Mars counts Mercury as an enemy, and the signs sit sixth and eighth from each other. In plain words, you act and then think, and Virgo thinks, checks, and then acts. Each can read the other as wrong when they are only different.

The tradition's answer is patience, which is the Aries catch in any case. Couples with this pair are said to do well when they split the work by strength: you start things and Virgo finishes them. And remember this is twelve points out of thirty-six. The birth stars can lift a low sign score a long way, and many happy couples sit on the hard side of a table like this.

sections.label: What signs cannot tell you
title: The other
twenty-four points.
paragraphs: The six remaining tests compare the two birth stars: temperament, instinct, health of the bond, the flow between you and more. Two people with the same pair of Moon signs can score very differently once the stars are counted. A full match also looks at each chart on its own, especially Mars, Venus and the seventh house.
So use this guide to understand a pull or a friction you already feel, not to rule anyone in or out. If the match matters to you, compare the two full charts.

steps.name: Choose the one who keeps up
steps.text: You are read as happiest with someone who has their own energy and their own opinions. A partner who always gives in feels easy for a month and dull after that.

steps.name: Slow down on the hard pairs
steps.text: With Taurus, Virgo or Capricorn, your speed is the usual source of trouble. Decide the big things together and give them the time they ask for before you move.

steps.name: Find both Moon signs before you judge
steps.text: Most people know their Sun sign only, and Vedic signs are counted from the stars, so the sign you think they are may not be the one that counts. Check both charts first.

faq.q: Is this by Sun sign or Moon sign?
faq.a: Moon sign, for both people. A Vedic match is made from the sign and the star the Moon was in at each birth. Your birth chart shows your Moon sign in a few seconds.

faq.q: My partner is a Virgo Moon. Is that bad?
faq.a: No. It is the lowest of the twelve on the two sign tests, which together are twelve points of thirty-six. The birth stars decide the rest, and the tradition's advice for this pair is patience and dividing the work by strength.

faq.q: How do I get a full compatibility reading?
faq.a: You need the date, time and place of birth for both people. With those, the two Moon positions give all eight tests. Draw both charts on the home page and ask about the match.

note: Planetary friendships are Parashara's natural ones and the sign distances are those of the classical eightfold match. Vedic (sidereal) astrology, Lahiri ayanamsa, read by Moon sign.
